newsitem.title: USA: Allstate sets growth strategy for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Allstate sets growth strategy for 1997.

text.p: Allstate Corp, which spent 1996 reorganizing its insurance operations in California and Florida while posting record profits, is preparing to expand its core insurance businesses in 1997, its chairman and chief executive officer told reporters in a press briefing on Wednesday.

"Our priority this year will be to grow our business faster-- which would mean a higher return for our shareholders-- and acquisitions if it looks like they fit," Jerry Choate told Reuters separately in a brief interview. "We're also getting more aggressive internationally."
Northbrook, Illinois-based Allstate, which reported net record profits of $2.1 billion, or $4.63 a share in 1996, has also launched a review of its agent system, Choate said in the briefing.
"The system that we're building will be driven by customer needs," he said, adding that Allstate will use the information in its database covering 90 million U.S. households.
"We need to be careful to keep up with what's happening with the consumer," Choate said. "We're willing to go wherever the consumer wants to go."
To achieve that goal, Allstate plans to add more agents this year, although Choate declined to provide exact figures.
"And you could wind up losing a lot of money on that real fast," Choate said.
Allstate's core business lines currently include property, liability, casualty, life and auto insurance coverage.
Meanwhile, Choate declined to comment on market speculation Allstate is planning a stock repurchase in 1997.
In November, Allstate's board approved extending the current repurchase plan by $750 million through 1997.

In a separate comment to Reuters, Choate added: "It's obvious we have a lot of excess capital, but our primary goal is to grow the business, take a look at potential acquisitions and if all else fails, we may consider a stock repurchase," he said.
Such policies are generally much more expensive than standard coverage, he said.
"It's the fastest growing segment and not a lot of people are good at (selling non-standard insurance)," he said.
Allstate created Deerbrook Insurance Co in 1995 to handle its non-standard business, now served by 1,000 independent insurance agencies selling policies on Deerbrook's behalf.

"It's important for the insurance industry to offer different (insurance) products to the market," Choate said. "Because if you don't, you risk having regulators stepping in and ordering companies to sell certain types of policies."
